incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title III — 'Des sociétés commerciales' — Articles L. 223-1 through L. 223-43 governing Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL), together with the application of Decree No. 67-236 of 23 March 1967 (Articles 25-72) and the French Civil Code on general contract validity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (single business formalities portal) operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), with transmission to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for entry in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 (déclaration de création d'entreprise) filed electronically via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, accompanied by the executed Statuts (Articles of Association) and supporting annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital is required for an SARL under French law; capital is freely set in the Statuts. At least 20% of cash contributions must be paid up upon subscription and the balance within five years (C. com. art. L. 223-7). Funds must be deposited in a blocked bank account or with a notary (dépôt des fonds) prior to registration, and released only upon issuance of the Kbis certificate. In-kind contributions must be fully paid up at subscription and valued by a commissaire aux apports.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the sole founder subscribes to the entire share capital, being [•] ordinary shares of EUR [•] nominal value each, fully paid in cash under Articles L.223-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code. RESOLVED that the registered office be fixed at [•], France, until lawfully relocated by the Gérant under the Statutes. RESOLVED that [•] be appointed Gérant for an indefinite term with full powers to operate the business of manufacturing and distributing underground tunnel boring machine spare parts, open bank accounts, hire employees and represent the Company before authorities. RESOLVED that the Gérant is authorized to publish the statutory legal notice, file the incorporation application on the INPI Guichet Unique and complete all related registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founder(s) in person or through a qualified notary (notaire) when contributions in kind are made; no government filing required for the deed itself.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statuts setting out the company name, corporate object exclusively covering the manufacture and distribution of spare parts and rotary cutters for underground tunnel boring machines (ISIC 2824 / NAICS 333120), registered office address, share capital structure, share transfer clauses, gérant appointment and corporate duration of 99 years. Each founder must initial every page and sign the final deed. If any contribution is made in kind, a commissaire aux apports must issue a valuation report annexed to the Statuts.
required_dossiers: Valid identity document (passport or national ID) of each partner
Certified French translation of any foreign-language documents
Draft and final executed Statuts
Commissaire aux apports valuation report (if in-kind contributions)
Proof of availability of the corporate name (INPI search certificate, optional but recommended)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the corporate name or corporate object is challenged by the registry or a third party, amend the Statuts by a rectificative deed (acte rectificatif) and re-execute before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of subscribed capital into a blocked account (dépôt des fonds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A French credit institution, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a notary exercising escrow duties.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the SARL 'en formation' and deposit the full amount of cash contributions, or at least 20% in accordance with Article L. 223-7 of the French Commercial Code. Obtain the certificat de dépôt des fonds from the depositary, stating the exact amount blocked, the subscribers and the undertaking that the funds will be released only upon RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Executed or draft Statuts
Power of attorney for any mandated signatory
Identity documents and KYC forms for all subscribers
Anti-money-laundering questionnaire and source-of-funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the beneficial ownership or source of funds, provide a reinforced KYC package and supporting bank statements; if the depositary refuses, select an alternative bank or notarial escrow and re-deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the statutory legal announcement (avis de constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized legal announcements newspaper (support d'annonces légales) of the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the publication notice containing the legal form (SARL), capital amount, registered office, corporate object, duration and identity of the Gérant. Submit the notice to the selected journal d'annonces légales and obtain the attestation de parution with the original published page.
required_dossiers: Project of the Statuts
Registered office address and proof of address
Identity of the appointed Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is returned for formal defects, correct the notice and republish; the attestation de parution remains valid for six months from publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic lodging of the incorporation dossier on the INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), automatically routed to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and sign the Form M0 online at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, upload the executed Statuts, the capital deposit certificate, the attestation de parution, proof of occupation of the registered office (lease or property title), the beneficial owner declaration, and the declaration of non-conviction of the Gérant. Pay the official fee electronically and retain the acknowledgement of receipt identifying the dossier number.
required_dossiers: Form M0 declaration (electronic)
Executed Statuts in PDF format
Certificat de dépôt des fonds from the depositary bank or notary
Attestation de parution in a legal announcements journal
Proof of occupation of the registered office (lease, sub-lease or title)
Declaration of beneficial owner (bénéficiaire effectif)
Declaration of non-conviction (attestation de non-condamnation) of the Gérant
Payment of the official filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises an anomaly or requests regularization, the missing documents must be supplied through the Guichet Unique within the notified deadline, typically 15 to 30 days; failure results in rejection, requiring a fresh filing and a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of the Kbis certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce in the jurisdiction of the registered office (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon transfer of the validated dossier from the INPI Guichet Unique, the greffe verifies the formal regularity of the Statuts, corporate name, object, and legal capacity of the Gérant. After approval, the company is registered in the RCS and the Extract Kbis is issued, evidencing the legal existence of the SARL. Retrieve the Kbis and the company identification number (SIREN), and open the permanent VAT and employment registrations.
required_dossiers: Complete M0 dossier transmitted by the INPI Guichet Unique
All validating annexes listed in Step 4
Proof of payment of the registry fee
Where applicable, the notary's certificate of subscription and payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe issues a provisional refusal or requests a judge ruling on the corporate name or object, cure the defect by amending the Statuts and refiling; if the objection concerns the Gérant's capacity, produce the missing court or administrative documents and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) — Inspection des Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE), under the authority of the Ministère de la Transition Écologique.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: ICPE operating clearance (récépissé de déclaration or arrêté d'enregistrement / arrêté d'autorisation) for mechanical metalworking and machining activities under the French Environmental Code, Book V, Title I, rubric 2515 and related rubrics.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Mission Régionale d'Autorité Environnementale (MRAe) / DREAL — Inspection des Installations Classées
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Rubric 2515 (mechanical machining of metals): 'Déclaration' regime when installed production capacity does not exceed 6 tons per day; 'Enregistrement' regime with a simplified environmental assessment when capacity exceeds 6 tons per day; 'Autorisation' with a full environmental impact assessment (étude d'impact) when the plant includes hazardous surface treatment, foundry operations, or solvent consumption exceeding the thresholds of rubric 2930 or Directive 1999/13/EC. For a tunnel boring machine spare parts plant, 'Enregistrement' is the baseline tier, with full EIA required in case of coating or heat-treatment units.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with the ministerial order of 2 February 1998 for ICPE: COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L, total hydrocarbons ≤ 10 mg/L, pH within 5.5-9.5, and no metal pollution (chromium, nickel, lead) above the prescribed analytical limits. VOC emissions from surface treatment or degreasing are governed by Directive 1999/13/EC transposed into the Environmental Code: solvent consumption ≥ 2 t/year triggers an emission reduction scheme with exhaust ELVs of ≤ 50 mg C/Nm³ in waste gases. Hazardous waste (oils, coolants, metallic sludge) must be registered and traceable under the bordereau de suivi de déchets regime.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) following an inspection of evacuation routes, fire zones, and extinguishing systems; structural load inspection by a qualified control body (bureau de contrôle) covering crane rails, mezzanines, and heavy machinery foundations; and occupational workplace clearance under the French Labour Code (Code du travail) covering ventilation, lighting, machinery guarding, lifting equipment periodic controls, and the registration of the plant to the CARSAT health-at-work service.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté Industrielle et Numérique, Paris; online business tax portal: impots.gouv.fr; company registration front-end: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (operated by INPI); non-resident VAT desk: DGFIP Direction des Non-Résidents, 10 rue du Centre, 93198 Noisy-le-Grand.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Submit the SARL incorporation file (statuts, identity and powers of the gérant, registered office proof) to the Guichet Unique (INPI) to obtain SIREN and SIRET numbers and the Kbis extract; issuance occurs within 4-7 business days. Step 2: For an entity established in France, the DGFIP automatically allocates the VAT identification number (FR + 11 digits) recorded in the SIRENE database; no separate application is required for domestic registration. Step 3: A foreign entity without a French establishment that makes taxable supplies in France must register directly with the DGFIP (Form Cerfa n° 13966*) and appoint a fiscal representative (Article 289 A CGI) when not resident in the EU; processing normally takes 3-8 weeks. Step 4: Where intra-EU B2B supplies exceed EUR 460,000 per year or intra-EU acquisitions exceed EUR 10,000, the entity must file the EC Sales List (recapitulative declaration) and monthly DEB/Intrastat returns. ISIC 2824 (TBM spare parts manufacturing) is not a licensed sector in France; no sector-specific tax permit is required beyond general registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A French SARL is by default a société de capitaux subject to Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) at the standard 25% rate (Article 219 CGI) on its annual profits; it is a separate legal person, a separate taxpayer and a separate VAT person (assujetti). Territorial scope per Article 209 CGI: IS is charged only on profits realized by establishments situated in France (strict territoriality); foreign permanent establishments are outside the French corporate tax net. Non-resident ownership is permitted and does not alter this classification; the SARL remains an entity-level taxpayer regardless of the residence of its shareholders. No tax-exempt zone status applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Election A - Fiscal transparency of the SARL (Article 239 bis AA CGI): a SARL exercising an industrial, commercial, artisanal or liberal activity, with fewer than 50 shareholders, shares not listed, and at least 50% of capital held by natural persons, may elect, irrevocably for a period of 5 fiscal years, to be taxed under the income-tax regime of sociétés de personnes, with profits taxed directly in the hands of the shareholders. Election B - Fiscal integration (Article 223 A CGI): a SARL holding at least 95% (directly or indirectly) of French subsidiaries may elect, with those subsidiaries, to form an integrated group neutralizing intra-group flows and offsetting group profits and losses in a single IS return. Election C - French VAT group (Article 257 C CGI): closely linked French entities may elect to form a single taxable person (assujetti unique) for VAT, eliminating VAT on internal transactions. Election D - No check-the-box regime exists in France; legal-form classification is mandatory and cannot be overridden by shareholder election. Hybrid-mismatch limitations (Articles 205 A and 212 bis A CGI, transposing ATAD) apply to interest deductibility and reverse-hybrid entities. No specific election is required for non-resident participation in a SARL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA) under Articles 256 to 289 C of the French General Tax Code (CGI), implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC; administered by the DGFIP, with customs clearance for exports handled by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis turnover threshold for VAT registration applies to businesses established in France: any person carrying out an independent supply of goods or services (Article 256 A CGI) must register and file TVA from the first transaction; for this SARL (manufacturer of TBM spare parts) registration is unconditional. The franchise en base de TVA (Article 293 B CGI) is an exemption scheme, not a registration threshold: enterprises with prior-year turnover below EUR 91,900 (supplies of goods) or EUR 36,800 (services) may elect to issue invoices without TVA and to file on the simplified regime; eligibility is lost in the current year when turnover exceeds EUR 101,000 (goods) or EUR 39,100 (services). This SARL, being B2B and export-driven, falls under the normal (real) TVA regime with monthly or quarterly returns. Non-established foreign suppliers: B2B supplies of goods are reverse-charged to the French business customer without the supplier being required to register; distance sales of goods to French consumers benefit from the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold under the OSS special scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has enacted a mandatory domestic B2B e-invoicing and e-reporting framework (Article 32 of the Loi de Finances 2023, as postponed by the Loi de Finances 2024): from 1 September 2026 all large enterprises and enterprises of intermediate size (ETI) must issue e-invoices and all VAT-taxable persons with a French establishment must receive e-invoices; from 1 September 2027 all small and medium enterprises (PME/TPE), including this SARL if classified as PME, must issue e-invoices. Mandatory channels are the public Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a certified private Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP), with data exchanged via API using the EU EN 16931 semantic model and formats Factur-X, UBL 2.1 or CII (with the French CIUS extension). France applies a data-transmission model, not a real-time clearance or pre-clearance model: there is no digital stamping or pre-invoice validation by the tax authority; invoice data plus payment-status data must be transmitted to the PPF either daily or no later than the 10th day of the following month, including e-reporting for B2C transactions and for international/export flows. Non-compliance (Article 289 quater CGI) gives rise to an administrative fine of EUR 15 per non-compliant invoice and EUR 250 per unreported transaction, capped at EUR 15,000 per calendar year per company.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Non-EU exports: supplies of goods physically exported outside the European Union are exempt with the right to deduct input VAT (effective 0% rate) under Article 262-I-1 CGI (exonération à l'exportation), provided the seller holds documentary evidence that the goods left EU customs territory within 90 days from dispatch or shipment (BOI-TVA-CHAMP-30-10-30) and that the export declaration (MRN) has been lodged with DGDDI. Intra-EU dispatches: transfers of TBM spare parts to a customer in another EU member state are zero-rated under Article 262 ter CGI, subject to validity of the customer's European VAT number (VIES confirmation), physical cross-border transport of the goods, and the seller's filing of the EC Sales List and DEB/Intrastat declarations. Ancillary offshore services (warranty, installation, site commissioning outside France) are zero-rated under Articles 259, 259 A and 262-1-2 CGI where they are directly linked to exported goods or are supplied to non-resident business customers, subject to the general B2B territorial rule (services taxed at the customer's place of establishment). The goods (HSN 8430/8431, TBM spare parts) are ordinary industrial goods not subject to export controls; no sector-specific license conditions affect eligibility. Export refund of excess input VAT is repayable by the DGFIP on the normal filing schedule, and for non-established taxpayers under the 13th VAT Directive procedure. FX repatriation: French exchange control (Code monétaire et financier, Articles L151-1 et seq.) imposes no fixed statutory repatriation deadline; export proceeds must be collected within contractual payment terms and settled through authorized French banks, while the decisive French VAT deadline for export proof is the 90-day physical-export window reflected in the field below.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (DAU - Document Administratif Unique) lodged via the DELTA-X/DELTA-G electronic customs platform with Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Transport document evidencing EU exit: Bill of Lading (connaissement maritime), Air Waybill (lettre de transport aérien) or CMR road consignment note
Commercial invoice (buyer and seller identification, HS/NC codes, Incoterms, export price, no TVA shown; mention 'Exonération TVA - Article 262 CGI')
Proof of payment: SWIFT inward remittance credit advice or letter-of-credit drawing documentation
For intra-EU dispatches: EC Sales List (recapitulative statement), DEB/Intrastat declaration and the buyer's VIES VAT-number validation screen
Certificate of origin (EUR.1 or ATR) where preferential tariff treatment is claimed (not VAT-substantive evidence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Assessment windows: DGFIP may reassess VAT within the standard 3-year period (Article L.169 LPF); the period is extended to 6 years where transactions relate to non-declared foreign establishments or undisclosed foreign accounts (Article L.169 B LPF), and to 10 years in cases of unreported foreign bank accounts or structures (Article L.169 C LPF). Clawback: if the export zero-rating is disallowed for failure to prove physical export within 90 days, for false or incomplete documentation, or for abusive use of the exemption, the full 20% TVA is assessed retroactively on the taxable amount, plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month (Article 1727 CGI), together with penalties graded by the taxpayer's good faith: 10% for good-faith late payment or omission, 40% for deliberate misdeclaration (mauvaise foi, Article 1729-1 CGI) and 80% for dissimulation, false documents or fraudulent manoeuvres (Article 1729-2 CGI). Criminal exposure: tax fraud under Article 1741 CGI carries a fine of up to EUR 500,000 and 5 years' imprisonment, increased to EUR 3,000,000 and 7 years for aggravated fraud committed by an organized gang or when the fraud attempts to conceal part of the sums due; the DGDDI may separately prosecute export-customs fraud and seize assets. No de minimis waiver exists in the export context; administrative tolerance is limited to documented cases of force majeure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) is the central bank and the authority administering the French balance-of-payments (Fichiers relatifs aux échanges avec l'étranger, FILEPA) statistical framework. Banking supervision and AML/KYC licensing of credit institutions and payment institutions is exercised by the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution), an independent authority legally attached to the BdF. The Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) at the Ministry of Economy and Finance retains residual foreign direct investment (FDI) screening powers for strategically listed sectors under Article L151-3 of the Code Monétaire et Financier (CMF). The subject entity is an SARL engaged in ISIC 2824 (tunnel boring machine spare parts), a non-screened sector, so no ex-ante Treasury authorization is required for non-EU shareholding, capital injection or intra-group financing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility. As a euro-area member, France transposed Articles 63-66 TFEU into the CMF (Articles L152-1 to L152-4), eliminating all approval-based exchange controls for current-account and capital-account operations. The Euro is a reserve currency with no convertibility restrictions. Remaining obligations are administrative and non-discretionary: (i) statistical reporting to BdF for payment flows with non-residents aggregating above EUR 50,000 per counterparty per month, filed by the banks under Article R152-4 CMF; (ii) CRS/FATCA disclosure on accounts of non-French tax residents; (iii) cash-courier declaration above EUR 10,000 (Regulation (EU) 2018/1672); and (iv) compliance with EU consolidated sanctions lists. Profit remittance (dividends) is fully convertible, but the paying French entity must apply the applicable withholding tax, reduced to 0-15% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive 2011/96/EU or the relevant income tax treaty upon submission of tax-residence attestations. No licensing, waiting period or central bank report approval is attached to any capital movement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. France abolished all statutory surrender and repatriation requirements for export proceeds. There is no mandatory conversion ratio and no deadline for repatriation. The FR SARL may invoice in any freely agreed currency (EUR, USD, CNY, etc.), retain 100% of export revenues offshore, maintain multi-currency accounts with French licensed banks, and select conversion timing wholly at its commercial discretion. The only mandatory duty is the monthly FILEPA statistical declaration by the bank (not an exchange-control approval) and the archival of supporting trade documents for five years. Export receipts are fully convertible at the prevailing market rate; ratio: 0%; holding period: unrestricted; surrender timeline: N/A. Under UCP 600 documentary credits, the collecting bank may condition payment on presentation of conforming shipping documents, but this is a documentary-condition framework, not a public exchange rule.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account in EUR; segregated USD/CNY multi-currency accounts; project-finance escrow account (compte séquestre) for EPC collars and retained earnings escrow
Operational Euro account; foreign-currency account (USD, GBP, CNY) for trade settlement; cash-collateral account securing Commercial LC and Standby LC issuance
Capital escrow account for shareholder equity injection and related-party subordinated loans; treasury money-market account for excess EUR liquidity
Trade finance back-office account; guarantee collateral account; intercompany project-financing account for overseas mining infrastructure disbursements
Secondary operational account for supplier payments, VAT clearing and payroll routing via SEPA CT
Restricted-purpose escrow account for tax/VAT deposits and statutory guarantee obligations

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: MEDIUM for treasury-only operational cash management (multi-currency IBANs, SEPA/SEPA Instant, API connectivity, FX sweep) using Qonto S.A., Shine (Swile), Anytime, Blank or Manager.one as secondary receivable-clearing accounts. LEGALLY CONSTRAINED as the primary treasury bank because a French payment institution (établissement de paiement under CMF Article L522-1) cannot: (i) issue or advise Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) or Standby LCs (ISP98); (ii) provide documentary collections anchored on bills of lading; (iii) originate FX derivatives or cross-currency forwards; (iv) hold third-party project-finance escrow deeds; and (v) itself file the monthly BdF FILEPA balance-of-payments report with full reserved data granularity. For a tunnelling spare-parts exporter relying on project financing and documentary trade rails, at least one ACPR-licensed full-service credit institution is mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is legally permitted under CMF Article R561-5-1 using electronic identification (eIDAS-qualified signature or video KYC through a licensed identification provider). In practice, for a standard-risk SARL with EU/EEA-resident gérants, fully remote onboarding with video interview is accepted by most Tier-1 banks. However, a physical interview (or a video interview followed by a one-time in-person meeting at the International Business Centre in Paris) is effectively required when: (a) any beneficial owner is tax resident outside the EU/EEA; (b) the capital injection originates from a non-EU source; or (c) the shareholding is held through an offshore chain. If the gérant is physically abroad, banks accept a French-resident legal representative holding a written mandate (procuration) dated less than 90 days before the meeting. Some banks also require a French-resident co-gérant for the dual-signature mandate when all shareholders are non-residents. No notarial deed is required for SARL account opening, but a notarized power of attorney is recommended for non-EU UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU beneficial ownership or an offshore holding chain that triggers enhanced due diligence and a 'source of wealth' investigation, with the bank demanding proof of the commercial origin of the funds used for the SARL capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate chain disclosed up to ultimate individuals; apostilled and French-translated tax-residence certificates for each UBO; signed source-of-wealth statement (salary slips, sale-of-shares deed, audited dividends) supporting the EUR funding; original bank reference letters from two issuing banks; RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filing certificate; and a notarized certificate of contribution (certificat de dépôt des fonds) proving the capital is genuinely subscribed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability of the non-French gérant to appear for identity verification, triggering a shell-company concealment red flag and standard refusal of account opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized power of attorney (Article 1366 French Civil Code) in favour of a French-resident legal representative; Kbis extract issued less than 90 days before; official passport and French residence permit of the UBO; INSEE avis de situation; VAT registration certificate; dual-signature mandate matrix; and a 6-month statement of the parent-entity operating account confirming commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening alert based on end-use in mining/tunnelling projects in sanctioned or politically exposed jurisdictions (e.g., Russia, Belarus, Iran), because cutter discs, hydraulic cylinders and gearboxes can be associated with extraction infrastructure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: List of contractual projects with geographic coordinates of the project site; end-user attestations (EUC) signed by the final project owner; commercial invoices with Incoterms proving delivery to a non-sanctioned site; dual-use self-assessment confirming the spare parts are outside Annex I of EU Regulation 2021/821; annual non-affiliation covenant with UBO signature; and the OFAC/EU sanctioned-party filter confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Freshly incorporated SARL with no audited financials and no French credit track record, causing the bank to request guarantees or a parent-company comfort letter before opening any overdraft or trade line.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year business plan with cash-flow forecast signed by the gérant; signed shareholder loan or equity commitment letter; three pro-forma purchase orders from EU customers evidencing industrial purpose; parent-company balance sheet if audited; expected monthly transaction volume and FX exposure summary; simplified due-diligence justification referencing the 'low-risk standard' classification of ISIC 2824.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Misclassification as a financial intermediary because the SARL collects project-financing drawdowns and disburses to subcontractors, which may be read as a payment service subject to CMF Article L521-1.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French counsel classification letter confirming the SARL is a manufacturing commercial company (APE 2824Z) holding only its own commercial receivables; company statutes prohibiting third-party payment processing; documentation that all funds are treasury balances arising from sale of goods; confirm that escrow arrangements are bank-operated, not client-held; and an internal policy statement that no client money is ever held.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for the equity injection from non-EU shareholders: (i) deliver the funds as a SWIFT MT103 (not MT202) to the dedicated EUR capital escrow account (IBAN FR76...), and in field 70 include 'INCREASE OF CORPORATE CAPITAL APPORTS' plus the SARL SIREN; (ii) for EU/EEA shareholders, the injection may be sent as SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001, ISO 20022) using the XML Purpose Code 'INTC' (intercompany payment); (iii) the French bank's collection platform requires a Banque de France 'code nature' mapping, so the SARL must select 'I. Direct Investment', nature 'A01 - subscription to capital' for equity, or 'CLTR'/'LOAN' for shareholder loans; (iv) before wiring, the SARL must file or update its RBE beneficial-ownership registration to mirror the change in capital structure; (v) the notarial or banking certificate of deposit (certificat de dépôt des fonds) releases the funds from escrow to the operating treasury account; (vi) no DG Trésor authorization is required since ISIC 2824 is outside the regulated FDI sectors, but when the origin is a high-risk jurisdiction the receiving bank will require the source-of-funds evidence described in the KYC defense dossier; (vii) all inflows above EUR 50,000 per month are captured in the bank-filed FILEPA declaration, while the client retains the definitive evidence (share-subscription deed, banking receipt, source-of-funds pack) for at least five years; (viii) any FX conversion leg must be separated from the principal wire into an independent deal ticket to maintain a clean audit trail in the central bank records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for the TBM spare-parts exporter: (1) Direct SWIFT MT103 for non-EU supplier payments — complete with commercial invoice, bill of lading or AWB, packing list and the French door-to-door ECS export declaration number; the bank applies the relevant EU purpose code (e.g., 'TRADE' or the tariff-driven mapping); (2) SWIFT MT103 with gpi (Global Payments Innovation) and mandatory UETR tracking for high-value payments, commissions or any flow into a jurisdiction with enhanced screening requirements; (3) Documentary Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP 600), at sight or deferred 90-120 days, issued by the French bank for procurement of forged cutter steel, hydraulic systems and electrical components from non-EU suppliers (notably China and South Korea), typically secured by a 30% cash margin or a banker's acceptance line; (4) Standby Letter of Credit (ISP98) issued in favour of EPC project owners to support performance and bid guarantees in tunnelling contracts; (5) Documentary Collections (URC 522) for medium-value spare parts, accompanied by EUR-1 certificates for preferential tariffs and certificate-of-origin forms; (6) SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT, pain.001) for all euro-denominated EU supplier settlements, payroll and VAT flows, with SEPA Instant for urgent disbursements. All trade payments above EUR 100,000 require matching of invoice, transport document and bank FX ticket to satisfy the 5-year documentary retention rule for BdF statistics. The SARL should maintain a segregated USD concentration account: export proceeds sweep into an overnight account and convert to EUR only upon specific treasury instruction, never by default auto-repatriation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD Outright FX Forward (change à terme ferme) — tenor 1-24 months, documented under the French AFB/CMT-003 convention or FBF master agreement; economically hedges USD-denominated TBM spare-part sale proceeds.

EUR/USD FX Swap (swap de change) — tenor 1-12 months, for managing the liquidity gap between USD export receipts and EUR operating needs; permitted as a commercial hedging instrument under the same CMT-003/FBF master.

EUR/CNY Outright Forward — tenor up to 12 months, available when backed by a commercial invoice for Chinese steel castings or hydraulic components; settlement via physical CNY where the bank offers CNY clearing, otherwise via Hong Kong/USD delivery.

Plain Vanilla FX Options (option de change) — EUR call/USD put and EUR put/USD call, tenor up to 12 months, executed as an OTC hedge under EMIR by a non-financial counterparty (NFC-) below the clearing threshold; speculative short option positions are prohibited by internal treasury policy.

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (swaps de taux et de change, CIRCUS) — tenor 3-5 years, permissible to align a euro-denominated project-financing facility with USD cash flows of an EPC tunnelling project; posted with variation margin if EMIR clearing threshold is exceeded.

Commodity-Linked Swap (steel or tungsten-carbide index) — available via the licensed bank or an EU investment firm, used to hedge raw-material price risk embedded in TBM cutter disc manufacture; qualifies as an ordinary hedging transaction under the French tax administration guidelines (BOI-BIC-CHG-50).

FX Collar (couloir cambiaire / tunnel) — combined put-and-call structure on EUR/USD for the minimum hedge ratio policy, executed as a zero-premium or cost-shared collar, limited to 6 instances per underlying commercial contract.

NDF for Exotic Currencies (RUB, TRY, EGP, NGN) — only exceptionally permissible when the SARL holds receivables from non-EU tunnelling projects in convertible-restricted currencies; booked through a licensed bank offshore booking venue; no NDF is applied to EUR primary pairs because the euro is fully convertible in France.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard CIT rate for fiscal years commencing on or after 1 January 2022)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% CIT rate for SMEs on the first EUR 42,500 of annual taxable profit, provided turnover is below EUR 10 million and the company is at least 75% owned by individuals; Research Tax Credit (Crédit d'Impôt Recherche, CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold; Young Innovative Company (JEI) status granting full CIT exemption for the first three profitable years and 50% exemption for the following three years; no manufacturing-specific tax holiday applies to ISIC 2824 tunnel boring machine spare parts.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory expiry; annual deduction capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income exceeding EUR 1,000,000; optional one-year carry-back of losses up to EUR 1,000,000)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa Form 2065 (Bénéfices industriels et commerciaux) together with the full liasse fiscale (schedules 2050 to 2058); mandatory electronic filing via TéléTVA / TDFC (www.tdfc.fr) portal through the professional accounts module of impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; CIT is payable through four quarterly instalments due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with the balancing payment due on the filing deadline
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the annual return must be filed by 15 May of the following year where e-filing is used (statutory 5-month extension of the 3-month rule under Article 223-1 CGI); paper filing deadline is 30 April; instalment deadlines fall on the 15th of the relevant months

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit before income tax, after depreciation, provisions and all expenses booked in the SARL's French statutory accounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL is the French resident taxpayer; where the foreign shareholder exercises management, the entire French-entity result is still reportable and the share of profit attributable to the foreign head office must not be removed without a valid permanent establishment analysis

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after statutory add-backs and deductions, including non-deductible charges (e.g. excessive related-party fees, 1/3 of mixed car expenses) and exemptions (e.g. 40% dividend deduction under Article 216 CGI)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer pricing adjustments for purchases from foreign related suppliers must be included here; the French entity cannot shift profits to a foreign affiliate without arm's length justification

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax loss available for unlimited carry-forward; the loss is also used to compute the EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% annual carrying-forward deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the French SARL cannot be surrendered to or surrendered by a foreign parent; the loss remains within the French tax perimeter

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration confirming whether transfer pricing documentation was prepared and the annual volume of intercompany transactions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for French entities with turnover reaching EUR 400 million and a 25% or more participation in, or by, a foreign group entity; indication of controlled cross-border spare parts purchases and royalty payments

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the research tax credit for qualifying R&D performed in France, including prototype development and patentable innovations in boring cutting tools
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: R&D subcontracted to a foreign affiliate does not qualify; the credit is refundable in cash where the SARL has insufficient CIT absorption

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late return penalty of 10% of the assessed tax (Article 1728 CGI), increased to 20% where the return is filed more than 30 days after formal notice and 40% for bad faith, and to 80% for deliberate concealment or fraudulent manoeuvres (Article 1729 CGI); late-payment interest of 0.20% per month (Article 1727 CGI); minimum EUR 150 penalty for an incomplete liasse and a EUR 15,000 fixed fine for failure to deliver transfer pricing documentation under Article 223 quinquies B

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% withholding tax on dividends distributed to non-resident corporate shareholders (Articles 119-2 and 187-2 CGI); 12.8% final withholding tax for non-resident individuals qualifying under Article 119-2bis; complete exemption is available to EU parent companies holding at least 5% of the SARL's capital for two years under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Article 119ter CGI); treaty rates typically range from 0% to 15%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate (attestation de résidence fiscale) from the foreign tax authority and file Cerfa Form 5000 (demande d'application d'une convention fiscale) with the paying French entity; the payer must submit the documents to DGFiP - Service des Impôts des Entreprises (Division des Conventions et des Relations Internationales, 10 rue du Centre, Noisy-le-Grand), verified before the withholding is reduced at source; where the withholding was applied in full, the refund claim must be lodged by 31 December of the second year following the year of the levy; refunds normally issued within seven months, with statutory compensatory interest (intérêt moratoire) if delayed; anti-abuse screening applies under Article 119bis A and the Multilateral Instrument principal purpose test
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic law imposes no ordinary withholding tax on interest paid to unrelated non-residents and no ordinary withholding on patent or know-how royalties paid to non-residents; however, a 75% withholding tax applies to interest and royalties paid to entities established in non-cooperative states (ETNC); most French income tax treaties eliminate withholding on both interest and royalties outright; the EU Interest and Royalties Directive grants zero withholding for qualifying related-party payments

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 (gross annual turnover or total balance sheet for entities whose ultimate group is also large): French entities subject to CIT must prepare and, on request, provide the full transfer pricing documentation (Master File and Local File) where their annual turnover exceeds EUR 400 million and they hold directly or indirectly at least 25% of a foreign entity, or are themselves held 25% or more by a foreign group entity; Country-by-Country Reporting is required for ultimate French parents with consolidated group revenue of EUR 750 million or more
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime; substance is nonetheless enforced through the general anti-abuse rule (Article L.64 Livre des Procédures Fiscales), the concept of beneficial ownership, the abuse-of-law doctrine for letter-box entities, the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive, and the Pillar Two 15% global minimum tax; a French SARL that cannot demonstrate actual management, employees, premises and commercial functions cannot claim treaty or EU Directive benefits, and its existence may be recharacterised as a pure conduit

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of export revenues from TBM spare parts sales, non-invoicing of after-sales commissions, suppression of books and records, or maintaining undisclosed bank accounts in financing structures linked to project payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 1741 CGI: five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine, increased to seven years' imprisonment and EUR 1,000,000 fine for aggravated fraud carried out through an organised group or with cross-border concealment; civil reassessment carrying a 40% bad-faith penalty or 80% penalty for fraudulent manoeuvres (Article 1729 CGI) plus monthly late-payment interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may be criminally convicted, subjected to a travel ban (interdiction de quitter le territoire), disqualified from managing a company, and held jointly and severally liable for the SARL's tax debts under Article L.267 LPF where serious managerial fault caused the non-payment; civil restitution and seizure of personal assets may follow

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Purchase of spare part components from a related foreign manufacturer at inflated prices, unremunerated know-how contributions, payment of excessive royalties to a low-tax affiliate, or failure to file the mandatory 2058-D transfer pricing declaration; abuse of letters of credit to conceal round-tripping of funds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 57 CGI empowers DGFiP to recharacterise and reintegrate the shifted profit into the French tax base at arm's length, with a 40% penalty for unjustified documentation and, where the recipient is in a non-cooperative state, a penalty up to 150% of the recharacterised amount; interest accrues at 0.20% per month
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director who knowingly signed false or incomplete declarations exposes himself to criminal liability as principal or accomplice to fraudulent declaration; courts may order disqualification from commercial management and personal contribution to the corporate tax debt under Article L.267 LPF

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creation of the SARL as a société écran with a nominal registered office, no employees in France, no actual board or management decisions, no genuine manufacturing or distribution activity for ISIC 2824 spare parts, used solely to receive invoices and channel outbound dividends to foreign shareholders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of Article L.64 LPF permits the tax administration to disregard the sham entity and reattribute its income to the real beneficiaries; the abuse-of-right penalty amounts to 80% of the tax evaded; the entity may also be struck from the RCS and its tax and customs advantages revoked retroactively
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced: the sole shareholder-manager faces personal liability for all French CIT, withholding tax and VAT under Article L.267 LPF; fictitious domiciliation is a criminal offence punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and EUR 75,000 fine; travel bans and asset freezes can be ordered during the investigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Sanctions / Fraudulent Use of Payment Channels
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing project financing or letters of credit for tunnelling machine spare parts through sanctioned jurisdictions, using front companies to obscure the ultimate beneficiary of payments, failing to file the beneficial owner declaration (DNC) with the RCS, or omitting suspicious transaction reports to Tracfin when payments are inconsistent with the commercial substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering under Article 324-1 of the French Criminal Code carries five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine (aggravated form: ten years and EUR 750,000); ACPR and Tracfin may impose administrative sanctions including prohibition on operations, professional bans and pecuniary penalties of up to EUR 1 million for legal persons
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may be prosecuted as an accomplice to laundering, be personally fined, suffer confiscation of his own assets, be placed under judicial control with a ban on leaving French territory, and be subject to personal bankruptcy measures (faillite personnelle), including a permanent ban on managing any French company
